descriptive_title: Grade 1 Mathematics: Demonstrations — A First Look at Likelihood (D2.1-D2.2)
subject: Mathematics

curriculum_expectations.D2.1: use mathematical language, including the terms “impossible”, “possible”, and “certain”, to describe the likelihood of events happening, and use that likelihood to make predictions and informed decisions
curriculum_expectations.D2.2: make and test predictions about the likelihood that the categories in a data set from one population will have the same frequencies in data collected from a different population of the same size

unit_overview: A 5-day Grade 1 unit on likelihood (D2.1, D2.2) framed around 'Will It? Maybe!' — Lucky Lou the Loon and Maybe Mae the Cat. Day 1 introduces IMPOSSIBLE, POSSIBLE, CERTAIN. Day 2 sorts events by likelihood. Day 3 makes predictions. Day 4 tests predictions in a new group. Day 5 closes with a Likelihood Lab capstone. Each lesson includes an expanded_walkthrough.
unit_learning_goal: Children will use the terms IMPOSSIBLE, POSSIBLE, CERTAIN to describe likelihood, make predictions, and test those predictions in another group.

lesson_arc.big_idea: Some events CAN'T happen (impossible). Some MIGHT (possible). Some MUST (certain).
lesson_arc.student_learning_goal: I can name events as impossible, possible, or certain.
lesson_arc.one_line_summary: Lucky Lou tries silly events; children name them impossible / possible / certain.

lesson_arc.big_idea: We can SORT everyday events into THREE likelihood buckets: impossible, possible, certain.
lesson_arc.student_learning_goal: I can sort events into three likelihood groups.
lesson_arc.one_line_summary: Maybe Mae shows event cards; children sort them into the three buckets.

lesson_arc.big_idea: We can use likelihood to PREDICT what will happen. The MORE LIKELY thing is the BEST PREDICTION.
lesson_arc.student_learning_goal: I can use likelihood to predict.
lesson_arc.one_line_summary: Lucky predicts coin flips and dice rolls; children predict using likelihood.

lesson_arc.big_idea: We can TEST a prediction in a new group. The same prediction may give DIFFERENT results.
lesson_arc.student_learning_goal: I can test a prediction in a new group.
lesson_arc.one_line_summary: Maybe Mae predicts pet preferences; children test in another class.

lesson_arc.big_idea: Detectives use LIKELIHOOD to predict and TEST. The data tells us if our prediction was right.
lesson_arc.student_learning_goal: I can predict, test, and tell if my prediction was right.
lesson_arc.one_line_summary: Children run a 5-station Likelihood Lab and write what their prediction showed.

recurring_characters.name: Lucky Lou the Loon
recurring_characters.role: Lead character. A friendly Canadian loon detective who predicts events. Anchors all 5 lessons.
recurring_characters.visual_description: A young loon with bright eyes and a small detective hat, holding a magnifying glass over a coin or die. Curious and confident.

recurring_characters.name: Maybe Mae the Cat
recurring_characters.role: Lucky's partner. The 'maybe' character — embodies uncertainty and tests predictions. Cameo Lessons 2-5.
recurring_characters.visual_description: A small striped cat with a question-mark patch on her vest. Tilted head, considering pose. Holds a clipboard for predictions.

threaded_vocabulary.child_friendly_definition: How likely something is to happen.
To say what will happen before it happens.
To try and see if your prediction was right.

pedagogical_notes: Grade 1 likelihood is qualitative — no numerical probabilities. Just 3 terms.
Use everyday events students recognize: 'will it rain', 'will the coin land heads'.
Predictions are educated guesses, not always correct — name this explicitly.
Testing in a new group (D2.2) shows that predictions vary by population.
Connect to scientific thinking — predict, test, observe, revise.
canadian_context_notes: Use Canadian weather examples: 'snow in July' (impossible), 'rain in spring' (possible), 'maple leaves fall in fall' (certain).
Loonie and toonie coins for the coin flip.
Survey at school vs at home for predict-and-test contrast.
